proposal.utterance: Classify 'Abusus' (the right of abuse, in Roman-law property theory) in BFO terms.

entities.label: Abusus
entities.rationale: Abusus is a kind of legal entitlement (the right to alienate or destroy a thing) that inheres in a property-holder in virtue of their externally-grounded legal relationship to res. It is a species of LegalRight, which is already typed as a Role (BFO_0000023 subclass). Roles are specifically dependent continuants that are externally grounded — here grounded in the Roman-law institution of dominium. It is a class (a kind of right) rather than an individual, because any owner of property could instantiate it.

entities.label: Dominium
entities.rationale: Dominium (full Roman-law ownership) is the encompassing role of which Abusus, Usus, and Fructus are component entitlements. Typing it as a Role subclass provides the bearer-class for Abusus. Without it, the part-of relation from Abusus to Dominium cannot be stated. Minting it now avoids an open-world gap.

entities.label: RomanPropertyLaw
entities.rationale: Roman property law is the normative information content (a body of legal doctrine, copyable and instantiated in texts and legal systems) that provides the institutional grounding for Abusus. Typed as GDC because it is an information artifact / normative pattern that can be concretized in multiple bearers.

relations.rationale: Abusus is a specific kind of LegalRight; it inherits the Role typing of LegalRight and the inheres-in relation to a property-bearing agent.
Explicit BFO typing as Role, externally grounded in the Roman-law institution of dominium.
Dominium is the encompassing ownership role of which Abusus is a component part.

Abusus (right of alienation/destruction) is a part of Dominium (full ownership bundle); BFO part-of at the class level captures the classical Roman tripartite analysis: usus + fructus + abusus = dominium.
Abusus is a subclass of LegalRight, which is already in the working ontology as a BFO_0000023 Role.
Roman property law is a species of the existing LegalArchitecture class (a GDC normative framework), providing the institutional context that grounds the Abusus role.

open_questions: Should Abusus be an individual (a specific historical right-type in Roman law) rather than a class? If the analysis is restricted to the Roman-law concept as a unique doctrinal entity, it should be an individual; if it is meant to cover any instantiation of an 'abusus-type right' in any legal system, a class is correct.
Should Usus (right of use) and Fructus (right to fruits) also be minted as sibling subclasses of Dominium for completeness of the tripartite analysis?

Is the bearer of Abusus always a natural person (BFO_0000040 human organism) or can it also inhere in a legal person (institution)? This affects whether a separate LegalPerson class is needed as the domain of the inheres-in relation.

Should RomanPropertyLaw be typed as an individual (the specific historical body of law) rather than a class? It could be modeled as a specific GDC individual analogous to USConstitution already in the ontology.
proposal.rationale_summary: Abusus, the Roman-law entitlement to alienate or destroy one's property, is most naturally typed in BFO as a Role (BFO_0000023): it is a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in a property-holder, is externally grounded in the legal institution of dominium, and is realized when the owner exercises acts of alienation or destruction. It is classified as a subclass of the existing working:LegalRight class (itself a Role subclass), because any owner of a res under Roman law could bear it — making it a kind rather than a particular. To express the classical tripartite analysis (usus + fructus + abusus = dominium), working:Dominium is minted as the encompassing LegalRight role, and working:Abusus is related to it via BFO part-of. working:RomanPropertyLaw is minted as a GDC subclass of LegalArchitecture to capture the normative-framework grounding. Key open questions concern whether to treat Abusus and RomanPropertyLaw as individuals (like USConstitution in the existing ontology) and whether sibling rights Usus and Fructus should be co-minted.
